stampedlock-optimistic-read-concept-036.title: Use optimistic reads with StampedLock
stampedlock-optimistic-read-concept-036.short: Reduce read contention when writes are rare
stampedlock-optimistic-read-concept-036.summary: StampedLock supports optimistic reads that do not continuously hold a read lock.
stampedlock-optimistic-read-concept-036.why: Read-heavy shared state can sometimes avoid the contention of ordinary read locking.
stampedlock-optimistic-read-concept-036.tips: Validate the stamp after reading and retry under a read lock when validation fails.

classvalue-per-class-cache-concept-036.title: Store per-class values with ClassValue
classvalue-per-class-cache-concept-036.short: Associate cached data with each Class
classvalue-per-class-cache-concept-036.summary: ClassValue associates lazily computed values with individual Class objects.
classvalue-per-class-cache-concept-036.why: It expresses class-scoped associated data without manually maintaining a Map keyed by Class.
classvalue-per-class-cache-concept-036.tips: computeValue runs on demand, and remove allows a later lookup to recompute the value.

string-strip-indent-code-036.title: Remove common indentation from multiline text
string-strip-indent-code-036.summary: String.stripIndent removes incidental common leading whitespace from multiline text.
string-strip-indent-code-036.why: It helps normalize indentation that belongs to source formatting rather than the text itself.
string-strip-indent-code-036.tips: Check line indentation and trailing-line behavior for the input format you use.

closed-channel-exception-io-036.title: Operate on a closed channel
closed-channel-exception-io-036.short: Keep I/O inside the channel lifetime
closed-channel-exception-io-036.summary: ClosedChannelException occurs when an operation requiring an open channel is attempted after it has been closed.
closed-channel-exception-io-036.why: A channel cannot be reopened or reused after close.
closed-channel-exception-io-036.tips: Use try-with-resources to make ownership clear and avoid retaining references beyond their lifetime.

overlapping-file-lock-exception-036.title: Acquire overlapping file locks
overlapping-file-lock-exception-036.short: Avoid overlapping lock ranges in one JVM
overlapping-file-lock-exception-036.summary: OverlappingFileLockException can occur when code in the same JVM requests a file-lock range overlapping one already held.
overlapping-file-lock-exception-036.why: Overlapping ownership of the same locked region would be ambiguous.
overlapping-file-lock-exception-036.tips: Track held ranges and reliably release each FileLock before acquiring an overlapping one.

generic-array-creation-error-036.title: Create an array of a type variable
generic-array-creation-error-036.short: Generic arrays cannot be created directly
generic-array-creation-error-036.summary: Code such as new T[n] is illegal because a type variable does not provide the reified component type required by an array.
generic-array-creation-error-036.why: Arrays retain their component type at runtime while generic type arguments are erased.
generic-array-creation-error-036.tips: Prefer List<T>, or explicitly carry runtime type information when an array is truly required.

annotation-element-invalid-type-error-03.title: Use List as an annotation element type
annotation-element-invalid-type-error-03.short: Annotation elements allow only specific types
annotation-element-invalid-type-error-03.summary: Annotation element return types are restricted, so arbitrary types such as List<String> are not permitted.
annotation-element-invalid-type-error-03.why: Allowed types include primitives, String, Class, enums, annotations, and one-dimensional arrays of allowed types.
annotation-element-invalid-type-error-03.tips: Use an array of an allowed component type when an annotation needs multiple values.

varargs-heap-pollution-warning-036.title: Understand generic varargs warnings
varargs-heap-pollution-warning-036.short: Check the risk of heap pollution
varargs-heap-pollution-warning-036.summary: Generic varargs can trigger warnings because the varargs representation is an array and may permit heap pollution.
varargs-heap-pollution-warning-036.why: Erased generic information combined with reified arrays can undermine type safety.
varargs-heap-pollution-warning-036.tips: Use @SafeVarargs only when an eligible method implementation is actually safe from unsafe operations on the varargs array.

bigdecimal-equals-scale-trap-036.title: Compare BigDecimal values with equals
bigdecimal-equals-scale-trap-036.summary: BigDecimal.equals considers both numerical value and scale, so numerically equal values can compare unequal.
bigdecimal-equals-scale-trap-036.why: For example, 1.0 and 1.00 compare as numerically equal with compareTo but not with equals.
bigdecimal-equals-scale-trap-036.tips: Use compareTo for numerical ordering or numerical equality when scale should not matter.

stream-peek-side-effect-trap-036.title: Use Stream.peek for required side effects
stream-peek-side-effect-trap-036.short: Do not make peek part of program correctness
stream-peek-side-effect-trap-036.summary: peek is primarily for observing a stream pipeline and its action is not guaranteed to run once per source element in every optimized pipeline.
stream-peek-side-effect-trap-036.why: Streams are lazy and implementations may omit stages that are unnecessary for a terminal result.
stream-peek-side-effect-trap-036.tips: Express transformations with map or collection operations and perform required side effects explicitly.
